chapters.summary: God calls his people to turn back to him, gives the prophet a vision, and promises to restore Jerusalem.
keyPoints: The prophet calls the people to turn to God, promising that if they turn to him, he will turn to them.
The former generations and prophets have passed away, but the word of the LORD stands forever.
In a vision, God promises to rebuild the temple and the holy city.
chapters.application: When we lose our way in life, let us remember that God calls us to turn back to him - he will surely receive us and give us a new beginning.

chapters.summary: Zechariah sees a vision of a measuring line, declaring that Jerusalem will be rebuilt and protected; he calls the exiles to return home, and God promises to dwell among his people.
keyPoints: The vision of the measuring line: God will rebuild Jerusalem and measure out its boundaries, showing his careful care and his plan for the city.
Glorious presence: the LORD himself will be the glory in the midst of the city and will dwell among Israel, and many nations will join themselves to him.
Called to return: God commands his exiled people to flee from the land of the north, for he has already judged the nations that carried them away.
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, God will surely care for his people. Let us answer his call, break free from spiritual bondage, and trust that he is with us, so that we may be his witnesses.

chapters.summary: In a vision, Zechariah sees the high priest Joshua accused by Satan, but the LORD himself defends and cleanses him, giving him a promise and a calling.
keyPoints: Joshua stands before the LORD, with Satan standing at his right hand to accuse him.
The LORD rebukes Satan and commands that Joshua's filthy garments be removed and that he be clothed with rich robes.
The LORD promises Joshua that if he walks in God's ways, he will govern God's house and enjoy special access, and foretells the coming of the Branch.
chapters.application: When we are accused or weighed down by self-condemnation, let us remember that God has already cleansed us and clothed us with the robe of righteousness. Let us serve him faithfully with grateful hearts, walking in his ways at home and in the church.

chapters.summary: Zechariah sees a vision of a golden lampstand and two olive trees, through which God encourages Zerubbabel to rebuild the temple by relying on his Spirit, and declares that every mountain of obstacle will be leveled.
keyPoints: The vision of the golden lampstand symbolizes God's presence with Israel; the lampstand is fed with oil from the olive trees, showing that God supplies every need.
Zerubbabel is reminded that it is not by might nor by power, but by God's Spirit that the work will be accomplished, and that even a mountain of difficulty will become level ground.

Zerubbabel will complete the building of the temple with his own hands; the seven lamps represent the eyes of the LORD, ranging through the whole earth, showing that God watches over and guides everything.
chapters.application: When we face mountains in life, we often rely on our own strength, but God calls us to depend on his Spirit. Let us ask the Lord for faith to trust that he will remove every obstacle and accomplish his purpose.

chapters.summary: In a vision, Zechariah sees a flying scroll and a woman inside a measuring basket, symbolizing that God's curse and the sin of the world will be swept away.
keyPoints: The flying scroll represents God's curse on thieves and those who swear falsely, showing his righteous judgment.
The woman in the measuring basket symbolizes wickedness; she is carried away by two winged women to the land of Shinar, showing that sin will be removed.
The vision emphasizes that God will cleanse his people, remove their sin, and restore holiness.
chapters.application: God calls us to turn away from sin, and he will surely cleanse us. Let us examine our hearts, put away wrongdoing, and live holy lives.

chapters.summary: Zechariah sees a vision of four chariots, symbolizing God's judgment on the nations, and is commanded to crown Joshua, foreshadowing the coming of the Messiah and the rebuilding of the temple.
keyPoints: Four chariots go out from between two mountains of bronze, representing the four winds or spirits of God going out over all the earth to carry out judgment.
A crown is placed on Joshua's head, foreshadowing that the Messiah will be both king and priest, and will build the temple of the LORD.
People from far away will come and help build the temple, and the nations will join themselves to the LORD, fulfilling God's promise to Israel.
chapters.application: In the face of a troubled world, let us trust that God is sovereign over all things and will surely fulfill his promises. Let us take part in his spiritual building work with faith, watching and waiting for Christ's return.

chapters.summary: Zechariah 7 records the people's question about fasting; through the prophet, God responds by emphasizing that true worship consists of justice and mercy, not outward religious ritual.
keyPoints: The people ask whether they should keep fasting in the fifth month as before, and God points out that even their eating and drinking were never truly done for him.
God recalls how their forefathers were punished for refusing to hear the law and hardening their hearts to do evil.
The prophet calls the people to execute true justice and show mercy and compassion, and not to oppress the weak.
chapters.application: Let us not focus only on outward religious observance, but sincerely obey God, care for the needs of others, and live out justice and mercy - letting our faith take shape in everyday action.

chapters.summary: God promises to restore Jerusalem and bless his people, calling them to do justice and love mercy, that they may become a vessel of blessing to all nations.
keyPoints: God promises to return to Zion and dwell among his people, so that Jerusalem will be called the city of truth.
God will bless the remnant, causing the land to yield its abundance, and the house of Judah and the house of Israel will be comforted.
God calls his people to speak the truth and render true justice, to renounce evil scheming and false oaths, so that many peoples will come to join themselves to him.
chapters.application: In hard times, let us trust God's promise of restoration, treat others with honesty and justice, and let his presence be evident in our lives.

chapters.summary: This chapter foretells that God will judge the nations and send a humble king to bring salvation and peace, establishing peace over all the earth.
keyPoints: God judges the neighboring nations of Israel - Hadrach, Damascus, Tyre, and others - showing that he rules over all the nations.
God promises to protect Jerusalem, to cut off the chariot and the war horse, and to bring peace and salvation.
It is prophesied that a humble king will come riding on a donkey's colt, and his dominion will stretch from sea to sea, bringing freedom and blessing.
chapters.application: Let us wait humbly for God's salvation, trusting that he reigns even amid chaos, and let our lives bear witness to his peace, for he has promised us peace and hope.

chapters.summary: God promises to send the spring rain and gather his exiled people home, making them like mighty warriors in battle, strengthened by his loving care.
keyPoints: The people are to ask the LORD for rain, and he will send abundant showers for his people, giving them plenty.
God will gather his exiled people and bring them home, like a flock led back by its shepherd.
God will make the house of Judah like mighty warriors who overcome their enemies, because he is with them.
chapters.application: In hard times, let us ask God, and he will surely grant grace and strength. Let us trust his promises - he will lead us home and make us strong to overcome.

chapters.summary: This chapter uses the picture of a rejected shepherd to portray Israel's rebellion, foretelling that God will give them up, and pronouncing woe on the worthless shepherd.
keyPoints: God commands the prophet to shepherd the flock marked for slaughter, but the flock will not listen to the shepherd.
The prophet breaks his two staffs, Beauty and Bands, symbolizing the breaking of the covenant with Judah and Israel.
The worthless shepherd will meet with disaster, for God will punish the leader who abandons the flock.
chapters.application: Let us remember that God is our good shepherd, and never let rebellion cost us his protection. Let us respond to his leading with obedience, and treasure the grace and peace he gives.

chapters.summary: God promises to protect Jerusalem, giving the leaders and people of Judah victory in battle, and pours out a spirit of grace and supplication, so that the whole house of Israel will look on the one they pierced.
keyPoints: The LORD declares that he is the one who stretched out the heavens, laid the foundations of the earth, and formed the spirit of man within him, and that he will make Jerusalem a cup that sends the surrounding nations reeling.
God will make the leaders of Judah like a firepot among wood, consuming the nations all around, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem will find their strength in the LORD of hosts, their God.
God will pour out on the house of David and the people of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and supplication, and they will look on him whom they have pierced and mourn for him.
chapters.application: In hard times, let us remember that God reigns over all things and will surely protect his people. May we keep humble hearts, look to Jesus Christ, and receive his grace, that we may find spiritual strength.

chapters.summary: The LORD promises that in the last days he will open a fountain for Israel to wash away sin, will wipe out idols and false prophets, and foretells that the shepherd will be struck down and the remnant refined.
keyPoints: A fountain is opened to wash away sin and uncleanness, symbolizing forgiveness and cleansing.
Idols, false prophets, and the unclean spirit are removed from the land, purifying the people's worship.
The shepherd is struck down and the sheep are scattered, and the remnant is refined through fire like silver and gold.
chapters.application: God is willing to wash away our sin, and he also refines us through the circumstances of life. Let us face him honestly, accept his cleansing, and hold fast to our faith through trials, becoming his treasured people.

chapters.summary: On the day of the LORD, Jerusalem will be besieged, but God himself will come down to defend the city, bringing judgment and salvation, and will establish his eternal kingdom.
keyPoints: On the day of the LORD, all the nations gather to attack Jerusalem; the city is captured and the people are taken into exile.
The LORD comes down and stands on the mount of Olives, which splits in two, opening a way of escape for his people.
God becomes king over all the earth; the holy city is exalted, the nations come to worship, and everything is made holy.
chapters.application: In the face of the world's turmoil and trouble, let us firmly believe that God governs history and will carry out salvation and judgment in the last days. Let us live holy lives, ready to meet that day, and wait for the coming of his kingdom with hope and faith.
